diagnostic_evidence.quote: Note that the space depends on $\left\{{\mathcal S}^X_d\right\}_{d\in \mathbb N }$, $\left\{{\mathcal S}^Y_m\right\}_{m \in \mathbb N}$, even if not emphasized in the notation.
Moreover, taking ${\mathcal E}^X=I$ (on $X$), ${\mathcal D}^Y=I$ (on $Y$) all spaces trivially collapse in the finite-dimensional case, proving \eqref{eq:CkBmuc(X,Y)=Ckw-eq}.

issues.failure_explanation: Taking identity encoders and decoders shows that every finite-dimensional map is cylindrical, but it does not establish membership in $C^{k;p}_{B,\mu,CC}$, whose definition uses a previously fixed BAP approximation scheme and requires $F_{d,m}\to F$ in the weighted norm. That convergence can fail for general finite measures. For example, on $X=Y=\mathbb R$, one may take the valid BAP scheme $S_d=(1+1/d)I$, an atomic finite measure supported at widely separated points $x_d$, and a smooth function vanishing with its derivatives at every $x_d$ but having weighted spikes at $(1+1/d)x_d$. Then $F$ has finite, even zero, sampled Sobolev norm, while the error of $F\circ S_d$ has a fixed positive contribution at $x_d$ and does not converge to zero.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify that, in the finite-dimensional occurrence of $C^{k;p}_{B,\mu,CC}$, the approximation scheme is the constant identity scheme, or remove $C^{k;p}_{B,\mu,CC}$ from the displayed equality.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted identification of all five finite-dimensional spaces is false for an arbitrary fixed BAP scheme; the reverse norm inequality and the other scheme-independent identifications are unaffected.
issues.title: Finite-dimensional equality wrongly includes the scheme-dependent cylindrical-consistency space
issues.why_classification: A local qualification or deletion repairs the statement without changing the norm equivalence or any principal universal-approximation guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then, the definition is extended by induction for $k\in \mathbb N$, i.e. $D^{k,p}_{\gamma}(X,Y):=\{F\in D^{k-1,p}_{\gamma}(X,Y): D_{\gamma}F\in D^{k-1,p}_{\gamma}(X,\mathcal L_2(X_{\gamma},Y)\}$

Since $\mathcal L_2(X_{\gamma},Y)$ is separable, we have Bochner measurability. Moreover, using the fundamental theorem of calculus, if $F\in C_B^1(X,Y)$ then we have that it is ray absolutely continuous. Hence, the case $k=1$ follows.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes the first-order facts for $F$: measurability of $D_\gamma F$ and ray absolute continuity of $F$. For $k\geq2$, however, membership in $D^{k,p}_\gamma$ recursively requires the Hilbert–Schmidt-valued map $D_\gamma F$ itself, and then its higher derivatives, to have the required stochastic Gâteaux differentiability and ray absolute continuity in Hilbert–Schmidt norm. Bastiani continuity gives continuity only after evaluation on fixed directions, so this does not follow merely by repeating the displayed measurability argument. A nontrivial trace-class domination argument is needed to pass from pointwise directional continuity to convergence and absolute continuity in the relevant Hilbert–Schmidt norms. Without that step, the inclusion in $D^{k,p}_\gamma$ and hence the completion and uncompleted equalities are unsupported.

failure_location.quote: According to definitions of spaces $D_{\gamma}^{k,p}(X,Y)$ in \cite{bogachev1998gaussian}, we iterate the argument to have the claim for arbitrary $k$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add and prove a recursive lemma showing that the restricted Bastiani derivatives define ray-absolutely-continuous, stochastically Gâteaux differentiable maps with values in the successive multilinear Hilbert–Schmidt spaces, using the trace-class Cameron–Martin embedding to obtain norm convergence; otherwise weaken the theorem by deleting the unsupported ambient-space inclusions and equalities.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed characterization of the new ambient and approximable spaces by classical Gaussian Sobolev spaces, especially $C^{k;p,2}_{B,\gamma,\eta,A}=C^{k;p,2}_{B,\gamma,\eta}$, is not proved. The later Gaussian EDA density corollary still has the separate direct route through the definition of $W^{k,p}_\gamma$.
issues.title: Gaussian characterization does not prove recursive Hilbert–Schmidt Sobolev differentiability
issues.why_classification: The repair requires a contained but nontrivial vector-valued differentiability and domination argument. Removing the claim would materially weaken the Gaussian characterization, though it would not destroy the paper's separate density theorem.
